costModel: $50 notes; each leg swaps through the pool's own liquidity (dy = L*dsqrtP, per-swap L from the Swap events) with the 0.30% fee and the vault's slippage guards; gas 920k units at 500 gwei priced in HSK (~$0.040); impact model "persist" (our price move persists; later swaps replay their exact input amounts on the shifted pool).

selectionRule: in-sample only: among configs with >= 15 in-sample notes, max(mean net P&L per note - 1 standard error); require > 0; then read out-of-sample once and keep it only if it made money after all costs
selection: best in-sample lower bound (catchup-k0.7-act12h-h12-all: -0.0438 - 0.0857 USD per note) is not above zero, so nothing was taken out of sample
notes: Replaying the live rules on 30 days of real HSKSwap swaps, the catch-up rule opened 110 notes (hit rate 19% against a mean break-even of 78%) and lost $19.91 ($0.181 per $50 note) after fees, impact and gas; momentum opened 90 (hit 8% vs 57%) and lost $17.69 ($0.197 per note), and every asset/kind cell lost money both in-sample and out-of-sample. The loss is structural: a round trip costs about 68 bps in pool fees and gas, plus price impact on these thin pools (a $50 trade moves WETH and WBTC about 16-18 bps and WHSK about 4.5 bps; execution impact averaged $0.095, $0.093 and $0.016 per note), while the pool itself rarely moves that far inside the horizon, so 78% of catch-up and 89% of momentum notes lapsed, most of them at about -$0.30 to -$0.34. A calibrated forecaster stating the true hit rate (0-20% per asset and kind) would have been refused by the vault on every one of these notes, since the contract requires stated odds of at least 50% and odds x (reward + risk) > risk + 60 bps. Of 88 alternative configs (80 declared up front, 8 fade variants added after every round-1 fade config fired zero times in-sample), the best in-sample lower bound was catchup-k0.7-act12h-h12-all at -0.044 USD per note (SE 0.086, 24 notes), not above zero, so no strategy is chosen (chosen = null): none of ours shows positive expectancy after costs on HSKSwap. The one regime with real pool-side catch-up, WHSK gaps of 200 bps or more while the pool was trading, is essentially one re-pricing episode (Oct 15-16, after the six-day dormant stretch), far too little to call a strategy. Limits: one 30-day window, the exchange mid is the mean of Gate.io and HashKey Global 5-minute closes and also stands in for the Chainlink seatbelt, settlement is checked every 30 s, and the persistence of our own price impact is modelled two ways (results similar, see sensitivity).
